description: Ranged chaos caster - rolling periodic damage drives Anomaly Spikes, stacking haste and cooldown resets, which cash out through the Incarnation of Chaos window.
_source_note: Built from reference/coa_sidekick/SPEC_chronomancer__infinite.txt: 'Closest to an Affliction/Destruction Warlock hybrid rendered in chaos-and-time flavor.' The tree is shaped by that spec's own loop - 'Most of the work is sequencing your DoTs so Anomaly Spikes and the haste and cooldown procs are always rolling, then cashing that into the Incarnation of Chaos window' - so five of its twenty-three nodes are procs rather than flat stats, which is high for this codebase and deliberate. Stat priority is Spell Hit > Spell Power > Intellect > Crit > Spirit > Haste, and Spirit appears as high as it does because Gift of the Infinite Dragonflight converts it into both of the top two.

nodes.name: Warpstriker
nodes.description: Reduces the Mana cost of your spells by 2% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the cost of your spells by -5% and the chance for your spells to be dispelled by 10%.' Note the SIGN: talented_cost does cost * (1 - pct), so a POSITIVE value is the discount. Guardian's Seasoned Fighter shipped -0.03 here and makes its abilities 3% more expensive per rank.

nodes.name: Deconstruction
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Unmake by 1% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the critical strike chance of Unmake by 5%.'

nodes.name: Rippling Power
nodes.description: Increases your Spirit by 2% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA class tree: 'Increases your Spirit by 8%.' Spirit is the listed primary stat for all three specs, which is unusual for a cloth caster and is why this tree, like the other two, opens on it.

nodes.name: Impeccable Timing
nodes.description: Increases the damage of your periodic effects by 4% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA class tree: 'Your periodic damage and healing effects can now critically strike.' There is no can-DoTs-crit switch (DoT ticks never roll a crit in combat/status_effects.py), so the node buys the same thing the switch would: more damage out of the ticks.

nodes.name: Anomaly Spikes
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 12% chance to launch an Anomaly Spike at your target.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Periodic damage dealt now has a 8% chance to launch an Anomaly Spike at your target.' The real mechanic, via the engine's cast_ability proc payload - it fires the spell free (Ability.use(free=True)). It triggers off DAMAGING CASTS rather than off DoT ticks, because on_damage_cast is a trigger the engine dispatches and a per-tick trigger is not.

nodes.name: Mind Melt
nodes.description: Your damaging spells weaken the target's attacks for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by Melt Reality now also reduces the target's primary attributes by -3%, stacking 5 times.' Attack power is the only outgoing-damage stat a Monster reads off a status effect, so the attribute shred is that; stacking is not available to a proc payload.

nodes.name: Gift of the Infinite Dragonflight
nodes.description: Grants spell damage equal to 4% of your Spirit, and 1 spell hit rating, per rank.
nodes._source: CoA's level-20 free passive: 'Increases your spell damage by 40% of your Spirit and your spell hit rating by 3% of your Spirit.' A real <target>_from_<source>_pct conversion, resolved against the shared STAT_CONVERSION maps in character.py. The hit half cannot be a conversion - hit_rating is a local feeding base_miss_chance_*, not a Character attribute - so it is flat, the same compromise Guardian's Bulwark made.

nodes.name: Distorted Time
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Timerend by 1 turn and increases the duration of Decomposition by 1 turn, per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the cooldown of Timerend by -2 sec and increases the duration of Decomposition by 3 sec.' ability_<id>_<stat> keys are built by interpolation in abilities.py, which is why a literal grep calls them dead.

nodes.name: Hourglass of Eternity
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 10% chance to grant you 10 haste for 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Periodic damage dealt now has a 5% chance to grant you 25% increased haste for 5 seconds.' Same per-tick to per-cast move as Anomaly Spikes, same reason.

nodes.name: Magic Erosion
nodes.description: Increases your Arcane spell damage by 2% and grants 1 spell hit rating per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Decomposition now applies Magic Erosion to the target, increasing attackers chance to hit the target with spells by 3%.' A hit-taken debuff has no reader on Monster, so the node grants the caster the hit instead - the same outcome for the Chronomancer, and honest about who it applies to.

nodes.name: Crown of Power
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Melt Reality by 5% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the tick rate of Melt Reality by -25%.' A DoT's effect_value is its TOTAL across the duration here, so a faster tick rate and more damage are the same number.

nodes.name: Shifting Chaos
nodes.description: Your damaging spells spill a tenth of their damage onto up to 3 other enemies.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Chromatic Shard and Anomaly Spikes now deal an additional 20% their damage dealt as Chromatic Damage all nearby enemies', and Melt Reality's own 'periodic damage dealt to the target is replicated for 20% of the value to all enemies near them'. splash_damage is the engine's real version of exactly this.

nodes.name: Black Hole
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Chromatic Shard and Unmake by 4% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the damage of Chromatic Shard, Melt Reality and Unmake by 15% against slowed enemies.' Nothing can read 'is the target slowed' at damage time, so the condition is dropped and the bonus is smaller to pay for always being on. Melt Reality is left out because Crown of Power already carries it.

nodes.name: Destabilize Time
nodes.description: Teaches Destabilize Time, which slows an enemy's actions and weakens its attacks.
nodes._source: CoA lists Destabilize Time as a spec talent, and the strengths section leans on it: 'Time Means Nothing and Destabilize Time amplify and slow the focus target.'

nodes.name: Infinite Power
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 25% chance to pull your damaging cooldowns forward by 1 turn.
nodes._source: CoA's level-10 free passive: 'Casting damaging spells now reduces your damaging spell cooldowns by 10% of their remaining cooldown', and the rotation note 'Infinite Power quietly pulls your cooldowns forward the more you cast, so never stop pressing damage'. The reset_cooldown proc payload takes a list of ability ids and a turn count, so this is the real mechanic rather than an approximation - percentage-of-remaining becomes a flat turn, which is the only granularity a turn engine has.

nodes.name: Timelost Power
nodes.description: Increases the damage your area spells deal by 5% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Discordance now strikes 3 additional enemies.' An ability's max_targets is fixed at load time and no talent key changes it, so a wider cleave becomes a harder one.

nodes.name: Incarnation of Chaos
nodes.description: Teaches Incarnation of Chaos, a burst window that raises all your damage.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Burst hinges on Incarnation of Chaos.' The spec's one real cooldown, and the thing its whole proc engine is ramping toward.

nodes.name: Infinity Crash
nodes.description: Increases the damage of your spell critical strikes by 5% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the critical damage of Discordance and Chromatic Shard by 50%.' There is no per-ability crit damage key, so it is the spec's spell crit damage.

nodes.name: Time Means Nothing
nodes.description: Grants 6 spell penetration per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by Chromatic Shard now increases the target's spell damage taken by 10%.' A damage-taken debuff is inert against creatures (see the module docstring), but the ATTACKER's spell_penetration is subtracted from a target's resistance inside both Monster.take_damage and Character.take_damage, and it is a real talent bonus key (character.py reads bonuses['spell_penetration']). So this is the node that actually delivers Chromatic Shard's 'pierces immunities and resistances'.

nodes.name: Chaotic Time
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Melt Reality by 8% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'While Incarnation of Chaos is active, your Melt Reality deals 30% increased damage and replicates an additional 20%.' The during-Incarnation condition has no reader, so the bonus is unconditional and smaller.

nodes.name: Aeon Rend
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 20% chance to reset Chromatic Shard.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Chromatic Shard now has a 25% chance to strike again and incur no cooldown.' A full reset is the closest thing to a free extra cast, and reset_cooldown with no turn count is exactly that.

nodes.name: Null Orbs
nodes.description: Increases your spell critical strike chance by 1% and the damage of your spell critical strikes by 6% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Periodic critical damage dealt now has a 20% chance to grant Null Orbs ... Increases the critical damage of Chromatic Shard and Anomaly Spikes based on your spell critical strike rating.' A proc that scales off a rating it also grants is not expressible; the two stats it is made of are.

nodes.name: Infinite Keeper
nodes.description: Your periodic damage erupts, spilling a third of every damaging spell onto everything standing near it. +6% Arcane spell damage and +10% periodic damage.
nodes._source: Capstone. CoA: 'Using Unmake on an enemy affected by your Timerend now causes the enemy to erupt in a vortex of sand, dealing Chromatic Damage every 1 sec to up to 8 enemies for 6 seconds.' The two-spell combination gate cannot be read, so it is a periodic splash on a 3-turn internal cooldown - the vortex, without the setup.
